newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss city of Lausanne grumbles at Mobutu presence.
newsitem.headline: Swiss city of Lausanne grumbles at Mobutu presence.

text.p: The municipality of Lausanne, host to Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko who is undergoing cancer treatment, complained on Thursday that he was disturbing the tranquillity of the Swiss lakeside town.

The Swiss news agency ATS reported that the municipality, in a letter sent to the federal cabinet and the local government of Vaud canton (state), said it had not been consulted about Mobutu's arrival in mid-August or the latest extension of his visa by the Swiss foreign ministry last week.

Lausanne authorities also complained that the publicity surrounding Mobutu's presence was not good "for the reputation of the Olympic capital" and could "disturb public order". The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is based in Lausanne.
"We had never been consulted," ATS quoted mayor Jean-Jacques Schilt as saying.

Mobutu, one of Africa's longest-surviving strongmen, has been undergoing prostate cancer therapy in Switzerland after having an operation on August 22. He has been living at Lausanne's luxury Beau-Rivage Palace hotel with more than 20 aides and bodyguards.
Fierce fighting has been raging in his country between government troops and Tutsi rebels who have mounted what is seen as the biggest challenge yet to his rule.
